concerns.quote: deficiencies in the foundation training of paramedics

reports.title: Lauren Smith: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: An ecg reading was taken at 08:56 am when both the paramedic and technician were in attendance on Miss Smith. That ecg was abnormal. The ecg identified pathological Q waves in V1, V2 and V3, an isolated ST elevation in V2 and a positive AVR deflection. Although the rhythm was sinus rhythm, 3 abnormal indicators were clearly present on the ecg. In addition, the auto diagnostic monitor clearly recorded the ecg as abnormal and reported an anterior infarct which was available for attending paramedics.
concerns.hazard: incorrect ecg interpretation leading to missed acute myocardial infarction

concerns.quote: I am concerned that neither the paramedic nor the technician was able to interpret the ecg correctly and that neither paramedic appears to have noted or acted upon the auto diagnostic monitor report.
concerns.hazard: failure to act on abnormal ecg results

concerns.quote: Lauren Smith was informed that her observations and ecg were normal. This information was not correct, and it is likely that Lauren Smith based her decision not to attend hospital on this incorrect information.
concerns.hazard: miscommunication of ecg results influencing patient decision

concerns.quote: I am concerned that there has been no collective learning by West Midlands Ambulance Service following the death of [REDACTED]. There has been no action to address the learning gaps identified by WMAS own internal investigation report in respect of both the paramedic and technician.
concerns.hazard: absence of organisational learning from incident

links.explanation: Both reports highlight a lack of adequate training in interpreting 12‑lead ECGs among paramedics. The later case shows the same deficiency leading to missed ischemic signs.
links.earlier_quote: one of the paramedics who qualified in 2015 after a 2 year foundation degree gave evidence that he had never had any formal testing on interpretation of 12 lead ECG
links.later_quote: Paramedic [REDACTED] gave evidence at inquest that she'd never heard of Q waves before and didn't see the ST elevation on the ecg
